findings.claim: Scrum's empirical-process-control foundation (Transparency -> Inspection -> Adaptation as a causal chain)
findings.failure_mode: terminology from outside this edition attached to the source
findings.evidence: Deep ref L15, L31 and source L163: the 2020 Guide says Scrum is 'founded on empiricism and lean thinking'. The phrase 'empirical process control' does not occur in the 2020 source (it is earlier-edition vocabulary).
findings.fix: correct: Scrum's foundation in empiricism and lean thinking (Transparency -> Inspection -> Adaptation as a causal chain)

findings.claim: The Sprint Retrospective as Scrum's Adaptation event
findings.failure_mode: loosened attribution: assigns one pillar to one event
findings.evidence: Deep ref L35 and L100: 'Scrum combines four formal events for inspection and adaptation'; 'Each event in Scrum is a formal opportunity to inspect and adapt'. Deep L159: the Retrospective itself inspects ('The Scrum Team inspects how the last Sprint went'). The Guide does not name the Retrospective as the Adaptation event.
findings.fix: correct: The Sprint Retrospective as Scrum's inspect-and-adapt event for the team's own way of working

findings.claim: In AAR context: metrics from the event under review are inputs, not verdicts. The AAR's job is to understand what happened, not to score it.
findings.failure_mode: application rests on a premise the quoted passage does not carry
findings.evidence: Deep ref L113: the passage is about forecasting tools (burn-downs, burn-ups, cumulative flows) not replacing empiricism, and says 'Only what has already happened may be used for forward-looking decision making'. It says nothing about scoring or grading past performance.
findings.fix: correct: In AAR context: forecasts and targets set before the event do not settle what happened; only what actually happened can inform the next decision.

findings.claim: the AAR must route those to the level with authority, or the adaptation will not happen
findings.failure_mode: hardened claim: 'more difficult' becomes 'will not happen'
findings.evidence: Deep ref L41: 'Adaptation becomes more difficult when the people involved are not empowered or self-managing'.
findings.fix: correct: the AAR must route those to the level with authority, or the adaptation becomes harder to carry out.

findings.section: Questions to Ask During AAR, Phase 1
findings.claim: Has the container (Prime Directive, confidentiality rule) been set well enough that transparency is safe?
findings.failure_mode: unattributed borrow from another corpus source
findings.evidence: The Scrum Guide deep ref and source contain no Prime Directive. It is Norm Kerth's Retrospective Prime Directive, carried by approach-perfect-field-guide-scrum-events-deep.md L218 and L242 [BT].
findings.fix: correct: Has the container (for example Kerth's Retrospective Prime Directive, via the Approach Perfect field guide; a confidentiality rule) been set well enough that transparency is safe?

findings.claim: Scoring instead of inspecting: empiricism requires using only what has already happened to inform forward-looking decisions, not to grade the past
findings.failure_mode: guidance attributed to the source's concept that the source does not give
findings.evidence: Deep ref L31, L113: empiricism = 'knowledge comes from experience and making decisions based on what is observed'; 'Only what has already happened may be used for forward-looking decision making'. Nothing in the Guide addresses grading or scoring past performance.
findings.fix: correct: Scoring instead of inspecting: the metric is being used as a verdict rather than as evidence of what happened (the Guide's empiricism uses what has already happened to inform the next decision)

findings.claim: The Transparency pillar requires that "important decisions are based on the perceived state of its three formal artifacts" [V], and a single account is low-transparency
findings.failure_mode: descriptive sentence presented as a requirement and used for a conclusion it does not support
findings.evidence: Deep ref L37: 'With Scrum, important decisions are based on the perceived state of its three formal artifacts' is descriptive and about artifacts. The requirement the example needs is the pillar's first sentence: 'The emergent process and work must be visible to those performing the work as well as those receiving the work' [V].
findings.fix: correct: The Transparency pillar requires that "The emergent process and work must be visible to those performing the work as well as those receiving the work" [V], and a single account makes most of that work invisible

findings.claim: the Definition of Done for this sprint included a mandatory code-review gate
findings.failure_mode: concept misframed: DoD presented as per-Sprint
findings.evidence: Deep ref L210, L217: the DoD is 'a formal description of the state of the Increment when it meets the quality measures required for the product', set as an organisational standard or created by the team 'appropriate for the product'. It is not defined per Sprint.
findings.fix: correct: the team's Definition of Done included a mandatory code-review gate

findings.claim: Conflating the AAR's output with the event's outcome: a poor outcome does not mean poor process, and a good outcome does not mean good process.
findings.failure_mode: smuggled concept (outcome bias) with no backing in the deep ref
findings.evidence: No passage in the Scrum Guide deep ref or source addresses outcome versus process quality.

findings.claim: The DoD gate rule and the Sprint Review working-session rule are both [V] in the deep ref and are applied here as paraphrased concepts with their source section preserved.
findings.evidence: Distillation L18 and L28 quote both sentences verbatim with [V]; they are not paraphrased.
findings.fix: correct: ...are both [V] in the deep ref and are quoted verbatim with [V] in Key Concepts 4 and 9.

findings.claim: the causal chain (Transparency -> Inspection -> Adaptation) that gives the AAR's three-phase structure a principled foundation
findings.evidence: No source in play gives the AAR a three-phase structure: TC 25-20 deep ref L19/L52 has four steps, and this distillation's own question tables run Phases 0-5.
findings.fix: correct: that gives the AAR's inspect-then-adapt sequence a principled foundation

notes: All [V] quotations checked word for word against sources/converted/scrum-guide-2020.md and found exact (the elided 'the most impactful improvements... as soon as possible' at L84 is a fair ellipsis). Counts (five Retrospective inspection domains, three accountabilities) match. Integration rows checked: TC 25-20 four-step process (tc deep L19, L52), OPL Blameless Postmortem and psychological safety (OPL deep L237), Psychology 2e conformity / self-serving bias / FAE (psych deep L277, L289), SSDL feedback thinking (ssdl deep L111) all hold. Main pattern: several applied lines stretch the forecasting-vs-empiricism passage into an anti-scoring rule the Guide does not state (D003, D006).
